logline: Four generations of a Korean family navigate discrimination, survival, and identity across twentieth-century Japan and Cold War-era New York.

renewal.note: Two-season run concluded with Season 2 finale on October 11, 2024; Apple TV+ has not announced a third season as of June 2026.

bollymeter.basis: 97% on Rotten Tomatoes across 102 critics with no major dissent; the dual-timeline structure and Youn Yuh-jung's performance drew near-universal superlatives.

pull_quotes.text: A sweeping multigenerational epic that is as visually stunning as it is emotionally shattering.

seasons.review_body: Pachinko Season 1 arrived as a formal statement about what streaming prestige television could look like outside Hollywood. Showrunner Soo Hugh built the season around a dual-timeline structure - Japanese colonial Korea in the 1930s and late-1980s New York and Osaka - that critics called the show's structural masterstroke. The cinematography, moving between two visual registers without losing coherence, was singled out repeatedly. Youn Yuh-jung as elder Sunja became the season's gravity - critics who had reservations about pace or scope still carved out space to praise the performance. On IMDb the season settled at 8.5. The Rotten Tomatoes critics score of 97% from 102 reviews was sustained through the run, not just opening-week heat. Audience numbers were modest but the word-of-mouth quality signal was exceptional.

episode_reviews.title: Chapter One
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the dual-timeline engine and introduces Sunja as a young woman in 1930s Busan. Directors Justin Chon and Kogonada calibrate two visual languages in a single hour - the colour palette itself signals which era you are in before dialogue arrives.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The opening long-take tracking shot across decades of Korean history sets the visual ambition for everything that follows.

critic_note.text: A visually ravishing series opener that earns every minute of its runtime.

episode_reviews.title: Chapter Four
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A midpoint hour that tightens around the cost of survival and the choices that cannot be undone. The Japan storyline accelerates while the 1989 timeline deepens Solomon's sense of displacement - the episode crystallises the season's central tension between assimilation and identity.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A quiet scene in which Sunja and Isak's relationship silently shifts register - no dialogue needed.

critic_note.text: Pachinko weaves time with aching precision.

episode_reviews.title: Chapter Eight
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale lands both timelines on notes of grief and stubborn resilience rather than resolution. The final sequence - deliberate, quiet, earned - drew praise as among the year's best closing images on television.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Sunja's final act of defiance, wordless and irreversible, closes the season on exactly the register the show promised from episode one.

critic_note.text: One of the most moving season finales in recent television.

bollymeter.basis: 97% on Rotten Tomatoes with critics calling it a confident deepening of the first season's visual and emotional vocabulary.

pull_quotes.text: Pachinko's second season is an assured, devastating continuation of one of television's most ambitious dramas.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 carries the family into World War II and its aftermath, extending the story from Osaka under firebombing to the postwar scramble for survival. Critics noted that the show did not coast on Season 1 goodwill: the writing took sharper structural risks and the performances, particularly from the cast playing both younger and older versions of the same characters, held under greater narrative pressure. The war sequences were cited for not aestheticising violence - the horror is mundane, which makes it worse. The 1989 Solomon strand closes with an ambiguity that divided audience opinion but earned critic respect. The season finale on October 11, 2024 delivered what multiple outlets called the series' most emotionally complete hour.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 tightens the emotional focus and raises the stakes of both timelines; slightly less wonder than Season 1 but arguably more devastating.
